cases.name: a_nullable_string_tag_carries_a_value
cases.why: `ClusterId` is tag 0 and nullable with a null default, so it is absent unless set. Present, its payload is a compact nullable string — the tagged section exists only in flexible versions, so there is no legacy form to choose between.

cases.name: a_struct_tag_carries_a_value_and_the_string_tag_stays_absent
cases.why: `ReplicaState` arrives at v15 as tag 1 while tag 0 holds its null default. The struct's payload carries a tagged-field section of its own, nested inside an entry of this one.

cases.name: both_top_level_tags_carry_values
cases.why: Tag 0 is a length-prefixed string and tag 1 a struct, so the two entries are sized by different rules and must still land in ascending order.

cases.name: a_nested_struct_carries_its_own_tags
cases.why: `ReplicaDirectoryId` (uuid, tag 0) and `HighWatermark` (int64, tag 1, defaulting to int64 max) sit on a partition, not on the message. A struct's section is emitted by the same code as a message's, and this is the vector that says so.

cases.name: synthesized_populated_v4
cases.why: Every field this version declares, present and non-default: one element in every array, every nullable thing supplied. The defaults case leaves arrays empty, which hides every field of the struct the array would have held — a records field encoded with the wrong length prefix survived the whole corpus that way, because nothing ever reached the struct holding it.
